newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Tissue to stop Skin2 sales.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Tissue to stop Skin2 sales.

text.p: Advanced Tissue Sciences Inc Minday said it will discontinue sales of its Skin2 human skin tissue product line and focus all of its resources on its therapeutic products.

In a statement the company said Skin2 has been used mainly by cosmetic and household goods companies for in vitro testing of new materials and compounds for a variety of applications including eye and skin irritation.

The company said it expects to take a third quarter charge of approximately $1 million associated with the closure of the Skin2 business; however, the company said the charge is immaterial in relation to its substantial cash resources.

"We have been a leader in the in vitro testing market and have continuously broadened the applications of Skin2," the company said. "Despite our progress, the market for in vitro products has evolved slowly, necessitating this decision."
The company said it considered potential partners and will continue to consider expressions of interest in acquiring the business.

The company further reported that it will be able to redeploy most of the Skin2 employees into Dermagraft-related programs. Advanced Tissue Sciences' therapeutic products in development include Dermagraft-TC for severely burned patients, and Dermagraft for diabetic foot ulcers.

The company said its Premarket Approval Application for Dermagraft-TC is currently being reviewed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration under expedited review status. The company said it expects to submit a second PMA for Dermagraft for diabetic foot ulcers in late 1996, pending successful results from its pivotal clinical trial.
